An Arizona orthopedic surgeon was arrested at PortMiami on October 20, 2026, after U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers allegedly found controlled substances in his checked luggage as he prepared to board the cruise ship Norwegian Jewel, according to court records and multiple news reports.

Dr. Jacob Lee Henrichsen, 38, of Central, Arizona, was detained at Cruise Terminal B during an operation known as Operation Temptation, in which officers searched luggage before boarding. Officers allegedly found capsules, gummies, mints, lollipops, a vape pen, pills stamped with a Tesla logo and mushroom-branded chocolate bars in a hard-sided case, according to reports citing the arrest affidavit and court records.

Field tests allegedly indicated MDMA in several capsules, gummies and pills, weighing about 11.9 grams combined, along with nearly 305 grams of suspected THC products, including about 236 grams of gummies, and about 160 grams of mushroom-branded edibles, according to CruiseNews.io. A preliminary field test of the mushroom products indicated properties of LSD, although the corresponding possession charge identifies the substance as psilocybin, that report said.

Henrichsen faces three felony charges, including MDMA trafficking and possession of controlled substances, according to Miami-Dade court records cited in news reports. His bond was initially set at $40,000, and later court summaries listed a $10,000 bond and indicated he had been released, according to separate reports. His attorney entered a not-guilty plea and requested a jury trial.

At an October 21 hearing, his attorney, Orlando Rodriguez, argued that the reported weights overstated the drug content because the candies, gummies and chocolate contained substantial amounts of other ingredients, including sugar and water, according to reports.

Henrichsen works at Mount Graham Regional Medical Center in Safford, Arizona, according to news reports. The medical center said it was taking the allegations seriously, according to one report.

Two other Norwegian Jewel passengers traveling separately were also arrested at PortMiami that day on felony drug possession charges involving THC and were released on $2,500 bond each, according to reports. Authorities have not indicated that the three passengers knew one another or that their cases were connected.

Homeland Security Investigations determined the quantities did not meet the threshold for federal prosecution, and the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office took custody of Henrichsen and the seized items for prosecution under Florida law, according to CruiseNews.io.

All charges are allegations, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: CruiseNews.io; The Arizona Republic / azcentral.com; The Travel, citing WPLG and NBC 6; Mad About Cruises.

title: Arizona Surgeon Arrested at PortMiami After Alleged Drugs Found in Cruise Luggage
